The gods of Cathay put certain Heroes to the test, and only by gathering enough Waystone Fragments can one earn their favour.
High Elves live under extremely strict laws and codes of conduct, embracing a life of harmony, balance and inner peace. To let oneself be ruled by rage or desire is seen as a mark of weakness.

Elven culture is steeped in mysticism and magic, and the elves believe their gods are always around them, a part of them. Every action, every thought, and every deed made is connected to the gods in some way, and each elven action is itself an act of devotion.

High Elf Heroes bearing the name of Ulthuan must collect [[img:ui/skins/wh2_main_hef_high_elves/hef_waystone_pieces.png]][[/img]]Waystone Fragments to earn the favour of the gods they worship within the Ulthuan's Name system.

The Champion of Asuryan can perceive intersections and focal points on the battlefield invisible to mortal eyes. They know the hour of their own foreordained death, yet none seek to avoid it.

The Phoenix Guard are the wardens of the Shrine of Asuryan, a great pyramid temple within the Sea of Dreams. In its deepest chamber lies the Chamber of Days. It is said that the past, present, and future are inscribed upon its ancient walls in the script of flame. Legend holds that any visitor who comprehends the meaning of these carvings is forever cursed to know the hour of their own death. Phoenix Guard legions typically appear when battle rages fiercest and hope of victory is slimmest, for their unique gift allows them to perceive intersections and focal points on the battlefield invisible to mortal eyes. Every Phoenix Guard knows the hour of their own foreordained death, yet none seek to avoid it. Whether the battle ends in victory or defeat, life or death, the Phoenix Guard fight on without fear.

Basking in the generosity of their patron god, the Scholars of Hoeth uphold their faith in the face of danger, probing the mysteries of the Winds of Magic with unerring insight. Only a fool would claim there is nothing left to learn.

The Swordmasters of Hoeth are excellent warriors, their intellect allowing them to master the rigorous doctrines of the Swordmasters with ease; likewise, each Swordmaster masters the principles of magical knowledge to perfection. Yet they rarely waste their time memorizing battle magic, focusing instead on more important, harder-to-recall spells ill-suited to the battlefield. Within the Tower of Hoeth can be found a vast wealth of expertise in craft, magic, and war. Most scholars focus on mastering a single discipline, honing their skill to perfection. Even among the noble elf castes, it is rare for one to fully master a single discipline, let alone several - yet it is not entirely impossible. This is precisely what distinguishes the Swordmasters from ordinary scholars.

Who would want to live forever? Most, in truth, would not refuse...
The sacred fire of Asuryan purifies each of his devoted followers, rendering them immune to ordinary flame - though only those who have endured the baptism truly know what it feels like.
Who but those who already know their fate could stand firm before a sky darkened with arrows or the sight of some hideous monster?
Whether battle brings victory or defeat, life or death, the Chosen of Asuryan fight without fear, just as the heroes of old whom they have witnessed once did.
All who have glimpsed the secrets of time are forbidden to speak of them; all who would do so must swear a magical oath of silence that can never be undone.
The Phoenix Guard always appear where the fighting is fiercest and victory seems all but impossible, for their curse has already shown them the shape of the future and the moment of their own end.
Yet the aura of sacred power that surrounds them is terrible to behold - their eyes blaze with searing light, and the air about them thrums with the raw power of Asuryan.
When fate hangs upon a crucial turning point, the Chosen of Asuryan leave their shrine, marching to war as the Creator's representatives among the elves, bringing hope to his mortal children.
You are truly a paragon of virtue and good deeds, honoured Champion - blessings will surely soon fall upon those who embody such virtue.
The realms of Men share our cause and must not fall! Our fates are intertwined, and their strength and devotion shall stand as steadfast allies to the people of Ulthuan.
Among all the 'younger races,' it is the Lizardmen who hold Asuryan in the highest regard - and that alone is enough to draw these cold-blooded Guardians of the World closer to us.

In these troubled times in the East, amid an age of darkness and discord, the Celestial Empire of Cathay must stand shoulder to shoulder with the sons of Asur against our foes - such is the decree of the Dragon God.
Even the Longbeards would set aside their Book of Grudges to welcome us for a time, and an ally's doubts and fears would dissolve like mist upon the wind.
The mage summons healing energy from the earth, sheltering warriors with nature's own restorative power drawn from the soil.
Hoeth is Asur's god of wisdom, and the patron of all who pursue knowledge - and the mage traditions of Saphery are unrivalled among the High Elf realms.
This one is deeply versed in the customs and culture of both Asur and Druchii, holds a position of importance within the White Tower of Hoeth, and is renowned throughout the High Elf realms.
The realms of Men must never fall - our fates are intertwined, and should they fall, we shall draw what lessons we can from their defeat.
These cold-blooded creatures have fought alone in the jungles for far too long - I have heard the whispers of the dragon-tamers, and this too is the will of the Old Ones.
Those who once forced the sons of Asur to abandon the Old World should understand that old feuds must now be set aside - pointless vengeance and oaths will only destroy an entire race!
Even the barest fragments recorded upon the scrolls of the god of wisdom hold immense power - they drain the user's vitality even as they fill them with magic in an instant.
It seems even the White Tower was astonished to learn that these beasts possess a language of their own - but with what mindset must they revere the Dark Gods!

Whether they hail from the graveyard, the ocean, or the desert, these skeletal frames and walking corpses are all the same - what truly matters is whether the great magic of their master can be broken.
Daemons often covet the souls of elves, yet even among daemonkind there is no true unity - wisdom well applied will always reap richer rewards than a reckless, furious charge.
These savage beasts gnaw ceaselessly at the pillars of the world, and now even threaten the stability of Asur itself - that Prince of Yvresse will surely be willing to lend an ear.
Beneath the White Tower of Hoeth lies the forge where every swordmaster is made, and the blademasters who guard this lofty tower possess wisdom and dexterity beyond belief.
